content: For human bites, individuals who have previously received a one-time dose of Tdap should receive a 5 mL dose of Td intramuscularly (IM) every 10 years. For dog bites, the following medical therapies are recommended: Unvaccinated patients exposed to an animal suspected of having rabies: Adults: Administer rabies immune globulin at a dose of 20 International Units per kilogram (IU/kg) intramuscularly (IM). Infiltrate as much of the full dose as possible around the wound(s). The remaining dose should be given IM at an anatomical site distant from the site of vaccine administration. Additionally, administer a 1 mL dose of rabies vaccine IM in the deltoid region as soon as possible after exposure. Repeat the rabies vaccine dose on days 3, 7, 14, and 28. Pediatrics: Administer rabies immune globulin at a dose of 20 IU/kg IM. Infiltrate as much of the full dose as possible around the wound(s). The remaining dose should be given IM at an anatomical site distant from the site of vaccine administration. Additionally, administer a 1 mL dose of rabies vaccine IM in the lateral thigh as soon as possible after exposure. Repeat the rabies vaccine dose on days 3, 7, 14, and 28. Vaccinated patients exposed to animals suspected of having rabies: Adults: Administer a 1 mL dose of rabies vaccine IM in the deltoid region as soon as possible after exposure. Repeat the dose 3 days later. Pediatrics: Administer a 1 mL dose of rabies vaccine IM in the lateral thigh as soon as possible after exposure. Repeat the dose 3 days later. For cat bites, monkey bites, rat bites, pig bites, and tick bites, medical therapy recommendations can be accessed by expanding the respective treatment categories.
